tasks.title: A scoped commit carries the journal row that names it
tasks.description: Every scoped commit writes the journal row naming it AFTER the commit, so the row is never inside it and no phase ends with a clean tree (reported by a user; visible on this repo at every phase end). Structural fix: write the row BEFORE the commit, keyed by a nonce the commit message carries as a trailer, stage it into the same commit, and resolve the SHA from the trailer (git log --grep) wherever a reader needs it - which also survives a rebase. Survey every reader of these rows (audit-journal, doctor, verify-invariants, the panel, journal-writes' record keys) and keep each one right; the hash chain must still verify.

tasks.title: audit-journal merge resolves the evidence ledger too, and a same-second tie over disjoint targets is ordered rather than refused
tasks.description: The evidence ledger is hash-chained like the journal and, before per-worktree writer keys, was appended on two branches under one name; audit-journal merge reads only the journal directory, so every such conflict was resolved by hand (interleave by timestamp, re-chain with the journal's row_hash). Give the evidence ledger the same merge verb the journal has - one implementation for both directories, the same refusals (a same-second tie that disagrees, a torn tail, a rewritten shared prefix), the same re-chain and a marker the evidence schema accepts (or a documented reason there is none) - and let a same-second tie whose rows touch disjoint targets be ordered deterministically instead of refused, with the order it chose written in the marker.

tasks.title: Review findings: a ledger tie is ordered only when latest_by_subject keys its rows apart, a squashed trailer still resolves, and the evidence merge names the row to stage
tasks.description:
Phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (R1) disjoint only when the rows differ under the (scope, subject) key with aliases that latest_by_subject uses AND under the _same_subject pair; red-first case for a --task run vs a phase sign-off run, and old-id vs moved id. (R2) match the trailer on the stripped line so squash and fixup bodies resolve; a case with a four-space-indented trailer. (R4) narrow the byte-identity claim to ledger files in code, docs and CHANGELOG. (R5) the merge output names the journal file carrying evidence.merge as a path to stage with the ledger, and g22 stages it and asserts a clone at the merge commit shows no drift. (R6) g21 asserts through the product reader, plus a cherry-picked nonce carried by two commits. (R7, pre-existing) an identical same-second tie is ordered by content too, so both sides give the same file. R3 as the review says.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_evidence_io.py:841-854: merge_target decides a ledger tie is disjoint using a subject rule no reader of the ledger uses. It returns 'task <taskId>' whenever taskId is set, whatever the scope. latest_by_subject (_evidence_io.py:1628) keys a row by (scope, taskId if scope=='task' else phaseId) and applies subject_aliases. Two cases get through as a result: (a) a `--task` run measured under the phase gate (scope 'phase' plus a taskId, which verdict_binding documents) and a phase sign-off run of the same phase in the same second; (b) runs recorded under a moved task's old id and its new id. merge_target calls both pairs disjoint, so the tie is ordered by content instead of refused. latest_by_subject then maps both rows to one key, and its `>=` tie rule means the LATER row wins, so the order the merge picked decides the phase's pointer. That is exactly the order-matters tie the refusal protected. This is judged from reading the code; no case exercises it. -> Treat two ledger rows as disjoint only if they differ under every subject rule a reader uses: the latest_by_subject (scope, subject) key and the _same_subject taskId/phaseId pair. A simpler option is to refuse whenever the two rows share a phaseId and either one is phase-scope. Add a red-first case pairing a scope:'phase'+taskId run with a phase sign-off run at the same second, and assert it is refused.
R2 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py:55-62 (claim at 17-20): commits_carrying only accepts a trailer line that STARTS with 'Audit-Row: '. `git merge --squash` (SQUASH_MSG) indents each squashed commit's body by four spaces, so after a squash-merge `--grep` finds the commit but the parser rejects every line and every nonce comes back unresolved. That shows up as a gap rather than a pass, which is the honest direction. But the comment says the row 'keeps naming the commit it is inside' after a rewrite, and that holds only for amend, rebase and cherry-pick. A `fixup` or a reword that drops the trailer has the same effect. -> Either match on `line.strip()` so an indented trailer line still resolves (a squash commit really does contain those rows), or name squash-merge and fixup in the comment and in the CHANGELOG entry as rewrites that leave a gap. Add a case either way.

The _scoped_commit module docstring still describes commit-manifest-index as '(the manifest INDEX, and nothing at all beside it)'. The build guide's commit-manifest-index section still says 'What it stages: the index, and nothing else. Not the shard, not the journal ... The allow-list is one entry long', a few lines above the paragraph this diff added saying it also carries the journal file holding its row. All three files are in P73.1's declared files. -> Reword all three to the shape the code has now: the index plus the one journal file holding the row that names the commit, and nothing else.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_journal_io.py:1672-1682 (and commit 04145ddf message): The _tie_faults docstring says the order rule is side-independent 'so both branches resolving the conflict produce the same file', and the commit message says 'both branches produce the same bytes'. For a ledger file that is true, because no marker row is written. For a journal file the marker row differs between the two resolutions: its ts is now, its actor is whoever ran it, and oursOnly/theirsOnly and the two input digests swap in its summary. mt1 compares only rows[:-1], so it checks the order and not the file. -> Say 'the same order of rows' for the journal and keep 'the same bytes' for the ledger only. Alternatively, make mt1's name and message state that it covers every row except the marker.
R5 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/audit-journal.py:750-757, 800-805; tools/check-git-pipeline.py:1760-1766: The evidence.merge row, which anchors the re-chained ledger bytes, goes to a journal file the operator is never told to stage. So the merge commit holds the re-chained ledger without its anchor. In a clone at that commit, the newest anchoring row for the ledger is one side's record() row, whose stateHash no longer matches, and that is the 'changed since' warning me2 asserts the row prevents. -> When res['recorded'] is True, name the journal file the row landed in and tell the operator to `git add` it with the ledger, or return it in --json. In g22, assert that the row file is named in the output, or that it is inside the merge commit once staged.

It never calls the product reader (_invariants.index_commits / commits_carrying), so the reader's record separator and prefix parsing are never run against a really rebased history (it3 covers amend only, in-process). Add an it-case that cherry-picks a trailer-carrying commit onto the same line and asserts both SHAs are returned and graded.

tasks.title: Round-2 review findings: a commit that absorbed a scoped commit is a named gap, never graded as the scoped commit
tasks.description:
Round-2 phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (R1) a commit is graded as a scoped commit only when its subject opens with its class's own header and the Audit-Row trailer is a line of its LAST paragraph, the stripped form still accepted there; a commit that carries the nonce any other way (a squash or any absorbing commit) is reported as a gap that names the absorbing commit, never graded and never a breach; cases for both directions, plus the squash probe from the review as a real-git case. (R2) the remaining index-alone sentences, including the user-facing breach sentence, say index plus the naming row. (R3) the DEFAULT_SUBJECT comment gives the reason that holds (readers find the class by journal rows and trailers) and cmi40 is replaced by a case that fails when a reader starts depending on the subject. (R4) newest_anchor's docstring claims only what it does. (R5) the refusal note names the shard that could not be read. (R6) a behavioural case for the tie only the verdict pair protects. (R7) the counted comments are reworded to carry no count.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py:437-441, 479 (commits_carrying strip); 570-573 (recorded_commits); 780-811 (index_scope grading): The R2 fix makes an indented trailer resolve, so after a real `git merge --squash` the squash commit is returned as the commit the row names. The scope checks then grade that commit's whole file list as if it were the scoped commit. I probed it by running code, not by reading (scratchpad/p73b/probe_squash.py, built on test__invariants' own fixture). On the side branch, a work commit plus a trailer-carrying index commit give index-scope `clean`. After `git merge --squash side && git commit --no-edit` on the base branch, index-scope reports `breach`: 'manifest-index commit b002dab9b2a8 staged src/a.py, and this class carries the manifest index ... and nothing else'. Before the strip, the same history was an unresolved-nonce gap. A squash whose bodies are NOT indented (a forge's squash message keeps each commit body) resolved the same way even before this fix, so the root is in P73.1's design and the strip only widened it. `_worktrees.py` treats a squash-merged branch as a normal workflow, so ordinary history now fails `verify-invariants` with exit 1. it8 asserts only commits_carrying's return value. No case asserts what a scope check says about a squash commit. -> A resolved commit is graded only when it IS the scoped commit. The test: its subject opens with the class's own header (`chore(audit-index): ` / `chore(audit-state): `) and the trailer is in its final paragraph. Otherwise another commit absorbed it (a squash), and the checker reports a gap that names that commit, rather than grading its file list. Add a case that squashes an index commit together with a work commit and asserts gap-not-breach. Add the pair case too: a squash of the index commit alone still resolves and is graded.
R2 (low) PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:150, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md:3100-3102, plugins/audit/reference/execute-task.md:529, plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py:807-811: R3's class is still open outside the sentences it named. (a) The tree line still says 'commits the manifest INDEX and NOTHING else'. (b) The guide's _scoped_commit section still says 'the other may stage only the shared index and never a phase's file'; that is the paragraph the fixed _scoped_commit docstring mirrors, and it also counts two commands where there are three. (c) execute-task.md says the script 'commits the index **alone**'. (d) index-scope's user-facing breach sentence says 'this class carries the manifest index (%s) and nothing else', while the reader beside it allows the journal directory. The commit's claim 3 says its grep covered governance/ only, which is why the docs and the printed sentence were missed. -> Reword all four to the index plus the one journal file holding the row that names the commit. Grep the docs and reference/ too, not only governance/.
R3 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-manifest-index.py:141-146; plugins/audit/tests/test_commit_manifest_index.py:604-621 (cmi40): The DEFAULT_SUBJECT comment says 'every reader finds this class by the `audit-index` SCOPE'. No product code reads the scope. index_commits/recorded_commits find the class through its journal rows: the `commit` field, or nonce to `Audit-Row` trailer. The only `--grep audit-index` is a person's. The conclusion is true (nothing reads the subject, so old commits are unaffected), but the basis given for it is not. cmi40 makes an empty commit by hand and asserts what git's own `log --grep` returns, plus a spelling pin (`'row naming it' in DEFAULT_SUBJECT`). No change to any reader could turn it red. -> State the real basis: the class is found through its journal rows, and a person finds it by the scope. If the old-subject claim is worth a case, run index_commits/index-scope over a history in which a row names a commit carrying the OLD subject, and assert that it resolves and is graded.
R4 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_journal_io.py:2702-2716 (newest_anchor docstring): The docstring says an evidence.merge row wins a same-second tie because its stateHash covers bytes 'which already include every run recorded against the file in that second'. That holds only for runs recorded BEFORE the merge. A record() row landing in ANOTHER journal file in the same second, after the merge, loses to the merge row, and verify reports drift. That is a loud false positive, not hidden drift. On the question asked: a forged same-second merge row in another file can now supersede a real record row. But a forged row one second later already won under both the old rule and the new one, so the rule adds no capability. Anyone who can append a valid chained row could always re-anchor. I checked with a probe that the choice is the same under every permutation of the candidates. -> Say 'every run recorded before it', and name the case of a same-second record after the merge as reporting drift. Optionally, prefer a merge row only for a target under the evidence directory, the only target record_merge writes.
R5 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_evidence_io.py:894-906 (plan_aliases): When a SHARD is unreadable, the refusal note names the index, not the file that failed. I probed a sharded plan with conflict markers in phases/P2.json. The note reads: 'the plan (docs/audit/audit-plan.json) could not be read (Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0))'. The operator is pointed at a file that parses, with a parser offset into a different one. The fail-safe direction is right: the tie is refused. -> Name the file that raised. For example, read the index and each shard separately in the except path, or say 'the plan or one of its shards' and include the shard path that failed.
R6 (low) plugins/audit/tests/test__evidence_io.py (em7-em12); plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_evidence_io.py:874-879: The `pair` target exists for commit-task-work's verdict_binding: `_same_subject` on the raw taskId/phaseId, with `_newest` giving a same-ts tie to the later row. The case it alone protects is a task-scope run and a phase-scope run carrying the same taskId, which have different subject_keys. No behavioural case covers that. em12 pins the exact tuple spelling, so a mutation that keeps the spelling but drops the pair where the key is present survives only by accident of em12's fixture. I probed it: the tie is refused today. -> Add a case that pairs a scope:'task' run with a scope:'phase' run carrying the same taskId at one second and asserts it is refused. Prove it red with merge_targets returning only the key.
R7 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-audit-state.py:211, 445, 450; plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-manifest-index.py:502; plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_scoped_commit.py:689; plugins/audit/scripts/governance/commit-task-work.py:734: The added comments write the scoped-commit cardinality into prose ('all three scoped commits share', 'two of the three lists', 'one of the three'). The lint does not match this shape, so it is author-enforced under CLAUDE.md. `_deps` already derives the writer set (every file defining COMMIT_TYPE and COMMIT_SCOPE), so these sentences go stale when a fourth class is added. -> Drop the numeral: 'every scoped commit shares', 'on the audit-state and task lists', and so on.

(T3) the gap names which test the carrier failed (subject header, or trailer outside the last paragraph) and says 'not in this history' only when no scoped carrier for that row resolved; a case for a genuine commit with an appended note paragraph and one for a row with both a squash and a reachable scoped commit. (T4, T5) the counted guide sentence and the stale test docstring reworded.
R1 (med) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py:627-628 (the `subject.startswith(header)` half of `scoped`); plugins/audit/tests/test__invariants.py:1688-1771 (it10-it13); tools/check-git-pipeline.py:1716-1778 (g23): No test enforces the header half of the new grading rule. The reason: every absorbing fixture squashes a branch whose index commit is the NEWEST commit. git's SQUASH_MSG lists commits newest first, so the trailer never lands in the last paragraph, and the inLast test alone makes the carrier absorbed. The case only the header decides is a side branch holding the index commit and then work (a follow-up fix after the index commit). I probed it (scratchpad/p73c/probe_carriers.py, P6): the index commit's indented trailer ends the squash message, so inLast is true, and only the subject 'Squashed commit of the following:' keeps the squash from being graded as a breach. Claim 2's '7/7 rows red' has no row for this half. -> Add an it14 with the P6 shape (index commit, then a work commit, then `git merge --squash`) and assert a gap naming the squash and no breach. tasks.description:
Round-4 phase review findings, all to be fixed. Orchestrator decisions: (V1) the gap's cause and ending are built from `failed`, not from one fixed sentence: a header failure names a squash or another absorbing commit as the likely cause; a last-paragraph failure alone (the subject carries the header) names a paragraph added after the trailer and makes NO claim that the commit is absent from this history; the ending no longer dangles; it16 asserts the absence claim is not made, proved red, and a case per failed-test combination. (V2) audit_state_commits and index_commits docstrings give the five-value return. (V3) the build guide states the grading rule: a carrier counts only when its subject opens with the class header and its trailer is in the last paragraph, and any other carrier is a gap naming it.
R1 (low) plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_invariants.py:686-692 (absorbed_gaps: the cause clause and the no-graded tail); plugins/audit/tests/test__invariants.py:1834-1841 (it16): The gap sentence reads `failed` only for the 'which test' clause. The cause clause is the same text for every entry: '- most often a squash merge that absorbed it, or a note added after the trailer'. The tail picks one of two sentences from `graded` alone. Probes on a scratch export of HEAD (scratchpad/p73d/probe_carriers_full.py) show two results that contradict what was observed. (a) P3 (a commit-msg hook appends a paragraph) and P4 (an amend adds a note) give failed == ['last'], and the subject DOES open with the header. The gap still says 'No carrier of it passed both tests, so the commit the row names is not in this history as a commit of its own'. But the carrier IS the commit the row names, carrying one extra paragraph. So the commit-message claim that 'a genuine commit that gained a note paragraph ... is no longer misdescribed' is not what the code prints. it16 checks the 'which test' clause, but not the absence of 'not in this history', so nothing would notice. (b) P6, P7, it14 and g24 give failed == ['header'] only. For them the offered cause 'a note added after the trailer' is impossible, because a note after the trailer fails the 'last' test, not the header test. My round-3 resolution ('say not in this history only when no scoped carrier resolved') left case (a) open, so this is partly a gap in my own earlier resolution. The direction is still loud: no-basis, never clean, never a hidden pass. The no-graded tail also ends in a dangling 'are not graded as its'. -> Build the cause and the tail from `failed` as well as `graded`. header only: 'a commit that absorbed it - a squash merge, most often - so the commit the row names is not in this history as a commit of its own'. last only: 'its subject is the class header, so this may be the scoped commit itself with a paragraph added after its trailer block (a hook or an amend); it was not graded', and make no absence claim. both: keep the squash reading. Finish the sentence ('...are not graded as that commit's'). Add `"not in this history" not in gap` to it16, and prove it red by forcing the absence tail back on.

It never states the grading rule this phase added: a carrier is graded only when its subject opens with the class header and the trailer is in its last paragraph, and a squash merge or any other carrier is a named gap, so the phase check answers no-basis. That rule is in the CHANGELOG and the _invariants docstrings only. A reader of the guide on a squash-merge workflow would expect the row to resolve and grade. -> Add one sentence after the `git log --grep` clause naming `_invariants.INDEX_HEADER`/`STATE_HEADER` and the last-paragraph test, and saying a carrier failing either is reported as a gap and never graded.
